question: Does the existing pinned lean-bench baseline guard flag a repeatable regression, rather than the discrepancy between independent-arm medians and adjacent-pair ratios in the original capture?
finding: Original full capture: approximation@10240 has independent-arm median change +16.8547300734%, while median adjacent-pair ratio is 1.0059734766. Other 135 parameters do not trigger the existing guard.
policy_source: lean-bench 8a37daf1074c3bdbd0da479b55538bad4a0022db, LeanBench/Export.lean compareParametric/perCallAtParam/classifyChange and Cli/Handlers.lean existing default 10.0 percent.
rule: Use each arms median of the three native per_call_nanos observations, for every shared parameter of every family. Strictly greater than 10 percent is a flagged regression. Also retain original adjacent-pair ratios as diagnostics; do not substitute those for the guard.
scope: All 17 families and all eight existing parameters, exactly the original three-trial AB/BA schedule and batch targets. No subset selection or timing threshold adjustment.
rerun: The one permitted unchanged full rerun after the inconclusive original cross-summary finding. Preserve both captures, including failures and all samples. No further unchanged reruns.
afterward: If a guard finding persists or moves, preserve it and investigate the actual benchmark/runtime bottleneck. Do not claim Phase6 accepted just because a pooled family median is near parity. A passing guard alone also does not discharge the separate declaration review or constitute fresh Phase4 scaling evidence.
sources: The exact original frozen binaries and source/toolchain identities in sources.json; byte-identical measurement script. Invocation directory metadata does not replace executable provenance.
host: Automatically leased CPU; shared-host load retained; no idle preflight, rejection, contamination threshold or quiet-core wait.
